arxiv-2102-11747.title: Uncertainty-aware Generalized Adaptive CycleGAN
arxiv-2102-11747.creator: Uddeshya Upadhyay, Yanbei Chen, Zeynep Akata
arxiv-2102-11747.description: Abstract Unpaired image-to-image translation refers to learning inter-image-domain mapping in an unsupervised manner. Existing methods often learn deterministic mappings without explicitly modelling the robustness to outliers or predictive uncertainty, leading to performance degradation when encountering unseen out-of-distribution (OOD) patterns at test time.

arxiv-2112-02696.title: Some remarks on semantics and expressiveness of the Sentential Calculus with Identity
arxiv-2112-02696.creator: Steffen Lewitzka
arxiv-2112-02696.description: Abstract Suszko’s Sentential Calculus with Identity 𝑆𝐶𝐼 \mathit{SCI} results from classical propositional calculus 𝐶𝑃𝐶 \mathit{CPC} by adding a new connective ≡ \equiv and axioms for identity φ ≡ ψ \varphi\equiv\psi (which we interpret here as ‘propositional identity’). We reformulate the original semantics of 𝑆𝐶𝐼 \mathit{SCI} in terms of Boolean prealgebras establishing a connection to ‘hyperintensional semantics’.

arxiv-2401-03489.title: Decentralized Federated Policy Gradient with Byzantine Fault-Tolerance and Provably Fast Convergence
arxiv-2401-03489.creator: Philip Jordan, Florian Grötschla, Flint Xiaofeng Fan, Roger Wattenhofer
arxiv-2401-03489.description: Abstract . In Federated Reinforcement Learning (FRL) , agents aim to collaboratively learn a common task, while each agent is acting in its local environment without exchanging raw trajectories. Existing approaches for FRL either (a) do not provide any fault-tolerance guarantees (against misbehaving agents), or (b) rely on a trusted central agent (a single point of failure) for aggregating updates.

arxiv-2401-16201.title: On Invariant subspace for hyponormal operators
arxiv-2401-16201.creator: Junfeng Liu
arxiv-2401-16201.description: Abstract . There is a resent paper claiming that every hyponormal operator which is not a multiple of the identity (operator) has a nontrivial hyperinvariant subspace. If this claim is true, then every hyponormal operator has a nontrivial invariant subspace, and every subnormal operator which is not multiple of the identity has a nontrivial hyperinvariant subspace.

arxiv-2402-01747.title: Existence and Uniqueness of Weak Solutions to Frictionless-Antiplane Contact Problems
arxiv-2402-01747.creator: Besma Fadlia, Mohamed Dalah, Delfim F. M. Torres *
arxiv-2402-01747.description: Abstract We investigate a quasi-static-antiplane contact problem, examining a thermo-electro-visco-elastic material with a friction law dependent on the slip rate, assuming that the foundation is electrically conductive. The mechanical problem is represented by a system of partial differential equations, and establishing its solution involves several key steps.

arxiv-2403-17684.title: Omega-categorical pseudofinite groups
arxiv-2403-17684.creator: Dugald Macpherson and Katrin Tent
arxiv-2403-17684.description: Abstract . We explore the interplay between ω \omega -categoricity and pseudofiniteness for groups, conjecturing that ω \omega -categorical pseudofinite groups are finite-by-abelian-by-finite. We show that the conjecture reduces to nilpotent p p -groups of class 2, and give a proof that several of the known examples of ω \omega -categorical p p -groups satisfy the conjecture.

arxiv-2405-11969.title: Sobolev regularity theory for stochastic reaction-diffusion-advection equations with spatially homogeneous colored noises and infinitesimal generators of subordinate Brownian motions
arxiv-2405-11969.creator: Jae-Hwan Choi, Beom-Seok Han, Daehan Park
arxiv-2405-11969.description: Abstract . This article investigates the existence, uniqueness, and regularity of solutions to nonlinear stochastic reaction-diffusion-advection equations (SRDAEs) with spatially homogeneous colored noises and infinitesimal generators of subordinate Brownian motions in mixed norm L q ​ ( L p ) L_{q}(L_{p}) -spaces.

arxiv-2406-11496.title: Decentralized Collaborative Pricing and Shunting for Multiple EV Charging Stations Based on Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2406-11496.creator: 1 st Tianhao Bu, 2 nd Hang Li ⋆, 3 rd Guojie Li
arxiv-2406-11496.description: Abstract The extraordinary electric vehicle (EV) popularization in the recent years has facilitated research studies in alleviating EV energy charging demand.Previous studies primarily focused on the optimizations over charging stations’ (CS) profit and EV users’ cost savings through charge/discharge scheduling events.

arxiv-2504-14416.title: Exploring Pseudo-Token Approaches in Transformer Neural Processes Equal contribution.
arxiv-2504-14416.creator: Jose Lara-Rangel, Nanze Chen, Fengzhe Zhang
arxiv-2504-14416.description: Abstract Neural Processes (NPs) have gained attention in meta-learning for their ability to quantify uncertainty, together with their rapid prediction and adaptability. However, traditional NPs are prone to underfitting. Transformer Neural Processes (TNPs) significantly outperform existing NPs, yet their applicability in real-world scenarios is hindered by their quadratic computational complexity relative to both context and target data points.

arxiv-2507-17216.title: The Pluralistic Moral Gap: Understanding Judgment and Value Differences between Humans and Large Language Models
arxiv-2507-17216.creator: Giuseppe Russo, Debora Nozza, Paul Röttger, Dirk Hovy
arxiv-2507-17216.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Giuseppe Russo, Debora Nozza, Paul Röttger, Dirk Hovy. People increasingly rely on Large Language Models (LLMs) for moral advice, which may influence humans’ decisions. Yet, little is known about how closely LLMs align with human moral judgments. To address this, we introduce the Moral Dilemma Dataset, a benchmark of 1,618 real-world moral dilemmas paired with a distribution of human moral judgments consisting of a binary evaluation and a free-text rationale.

europmc-pmc2600276.description: Virulence of and deaths from Clostridium difficile-associated disease (CDAD) are on the rise in the United States. plos-pone-0012172.creator: Matthew A. Schaller, Hannah Logue, Sumanta Mukherjee et al.
plos-pone-0012172.description: PLOS ONE research article. Studies have shown that Notch is essential for the maintenance of a T cell Th2 phenotype in vivo. It has also been shown that Notch ligands have diverse functions during T cell activation. We chose to investigate the role of Notch ligands during the Th2 response. We studied the r

pmc-10529519.title: A Machine Learning-Based Method for Detecting Liver Fibrosis
pmc-10529519.creator: Miguel Suárez, Raquel Martínez, Ana María Torres, Antonio Ramón, Pilar Blasco, Jorge Mateo, Henk A Marquering
pmc-10529519.description: Cholecystectomy and Metabolic-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) are prevalent conditions in gastroenterology, frequently co-occurring in clinical practice. Cholecystectomy has been shown to have metabolic consequences, sharing similar pathological mechanisms with MASLD. A database of MASLD patients who underwent cholecystectomy was analysed. This study aimed to develop a tool to identify the risk of liver fibrosis after cholecystectomy.

pmc-10660755.title: Perioperative Urinary Catheter Use and Association to (Gram-Negative) Surgical Site Infection after Spine Surgery
pmc-10660755.creator: Alexandre Ansorge, Michael Betz, Oliver Wetzel, Marco Dimitri Burkhard, Igor Dichovski, Mazda Farshad, Ilker Uçkay
pmc-10660755.description: This study evaluates potential associations between the perioperative urinary catheter (UC) carriage and (Gram-negative) surgical site infections (SSIs) after spine surgery. It is a retrospective, single-center, case-control study stratifying group comparisons, case-mix adjustments using multivariate logistic regression analyses. Around half of the patients (2734/5485 surgeries) carried a UC for 1 day (median duration) (interquartile range, 1–1 days).

pmc-11536961.title: The efficacy and safety of ketorolac for postoperative pain management in lumbar spine surgery: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
pmc-11536961.creator: Jianbin Guan, Ningning Feng, Kaitan Yang, Haimiti Abudouaini, Peng Liu
pmc-11536961.description: BackgroundKetorolac is widely utilized for postoperative pain management, including back pain after lumbar spinal surgery. Several trials have assessed the efficacy of Ketorolac alone and in combination with other analgesics such as bupivacaine, morphine, epinephrine, paracetamol, and pregabalin. However, the effects and safety profile of ketorolac in these contexts remain controversial.

pmc-11664484.title: Chemogenetic activation of astrocytes modulates sleep–wakefulness states in a brain region-dependent manner
pmc-11664484.creator: Yuta Kurogi, Tomomi Sanagi, Daisuke Ono, Tomomi Tsunematsu
pmc-11664484.description: Study ObjectivesAstrocytes change their intracellular calcium (Ca2+) concentration during sleep/wakefulness states in mice. Furthermore, the Ca2+ dynamics in astrocytes vary depending on the brain region. However, it remains unclear whether alterations in astrocyte activity can affect sleep–wake states and cortical oscillations in a brain region-dependent manner.MethodsAstrocyte activity was artificially manipulated in mice using chemogenetics.

pmc-11716899.title: The use of neural‐derived extracellular vesicles as a biomarker tool of neuropathology (with focus on Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia)
pmc-11716899.creator: Millie Sander, Esra Bozbas, Clive G Ballard
pmc-11716899.description: BackgroundEstablishing novel biomarkers to detect of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and Lewy body dementia (LBD) neuropathology is integral to support early diagnosis and the differentiation between dementia subtypes. Neural‐derived extracellular vesicles (NDEVs) – released by neural cells into circulation – provide promise in this regard.

pmc-12508721.title: Discovery of Surface‐Engineered Nanoparticles That Boost Enzyme Activity via High‐Throughput Screening and Machine Learning
pmc-12508721.creator: Yuanjie Sun, Subrata Pandit, Neha Satish, Gabriel Gilman, Dylan M Snider, Devleena Samanta
pmc-12508721.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Nanoparticles (NPs) are known to enhance the activity of enzymes, but such findings remain largely empirical, lacking predictive design principles. Here, the first high‐throughput platform for the discovery of surface‐engineered nanoparticles (SENs) that modulate enzyme function is introduced. Guided by the hypothesis that surface ligands are primary drivers of activity enhancement, a library of 194 gold‐ and palladium‐based SENs functionalized with diverse peptide ligands is synthesized. These SENs are screened against three model enzymes: cytochrome c, lactoperoxidase (LPO), and lipase.

pmc-12637348.title: Insulin resistance spawns hypertriglyceridemia-induced acute pancreatitis and diabetic ketoacidosis: an evolving metabolic cascade
pmc-12637348.creator: Chaoneng Wu, Apoorv Tiwari, Maxim Zlatopolsky, Omar Qaqish, William E. Harder, Sonela Blaceri, Chadi Saad, Sujata Kambhatla, Ashok Kondur
pmc-12637348.description: Insulin resistance (IR) is associated with uncontrolled lipolysis, leading to the release of free fatty acids, ectopic fat accumulation, and hypertriglyceridemia (HTG). Adipose IR is the primary factor contributing to severe HTG, which interacts with deregulated hepatic IR (Hep-IR), resulting in hypertriglyceridemic acute pancreatitis (HTGAP) and diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA).

pmc-13507343.title: In situ mapping of late-stage biomechanical coordination during clathrin-mediated endocytosis
pmc-13507343.creator: Bin Wu, Tian Luo, Yu Zhu, Xin Zhang, Dongliang Song, Yanling Lin, Yuanfang Sun, Teng-Xiang Huang, Xiaodong Cheng, Ning Fang
pmc-13507343.description: Clathrin-mediated endocytosis (CME) requires precise coordination between membrane deformation and force-generating protein assemblies, yet how these forces are dynamically organized in living cells remains poorly defined. Using multi-dimensional single particle tracking (SPT), we indirectly visualize the mechanical motions of individual clathrin-coated pits during the late stages of CME.

pmc-13530165.title: Base-catalyzed regioselective C(sp3)–Si bond activation of silacyclobutanes and benzosilacyclobutenes
pmc-13530165.creator: Yuanfang Kong, Delong Mu
pmc-13530165.description: The development of a green, sustainable, and environment-friendly activation model is of great significance in catalytic chemistry. Herein, a transition-metal- and ligand-free, base-catalyzed regioselective C(sp3)–Si bond activation of silacyclobutanes (SCBs) and benzosilacyclobutenes (BSBs) has been developed. The protocol features a simple catalytic system that proceeds smoothly under air atmosphere without requiring inert gas protection.

pmc-13644093.title: Enhancement of solubility and antioxidant activity of quercetin in choline-aspartate ionic liquid: spectroscopic, volumetric and kinetic insights
pmc-13644093.creator: Vibek Srichandan, Sanghamitra Pradhan, Malabika Talukdar
pmc-13644093.description: Quercetin is a biologically active flavonoid which has well established antioxidant properties, but its bioavailability and functional applicability are constrained due to its extremely poor aqueous solubility. In the present study, a biocompatible [Ch][Asp] IL was synthesized through a one pot metathesis neutralization route and investigated as a green functional medium for enhancing the solubility and scavenging activity of quercetin.

pmc-13682688.title: How Patients' Inquiry Shapes Meaning in Primary Care Consultations: A Qualitative Study Using Own‐Point‐of‐View Video‐Stimulated Recall
pmc-13682688.creator: Louis‐Baptiste Jaunay, Anne‐Sophie Ivanoff, Corentin Philippot, Emmanuel Triby, Thierry Pelaccia
pmc-13682688.description: RationaleMedical consultations are collaborative encounters in which physicians and patients jointly address health concerns and make decisions. While most research has focused on physicians' clinical reasoning, decision‐making is increasingly viewed as a form of situated cognition, distributed across individuals and their interactions. However, the patient's perspective on how they make sense of their health problems remains underexamined.

pmc-13690100.title: Psychosocial Effects of Hyperemesis Gravidarum: A Systematic Literature Review
pmc-13690100.creator: Abigail Veenstra, Jacob Lahti, Mahyar M Shabani, Thomas C Varkey
pmc-13690100.description: Objective:Hyperemesis gravidarum (HG) is a severe form of nausea and vomiting during pregnancy that can have significant physical consequences for the pregnant individual. However, studying affected patients often reveals an additional dimension of impact—specifically, the psychosocial effects on their quality of life.Materials and methods:This literature review was conducted following the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) guidelines.
